items.title: Vince DiMartino interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 8, 2025
items.q: Try to play along with Maynard Ferguson and I’m going, “They don’t even have the fingerings in the book for this, so how am I supposed to do this?”

ctx.x: You were trying to get what these trumpet players were playing?

Yes and I thought that I was like the worst trumpet player that ever lived, because I couldn’t play a lot of the stuff that was on the records. Try to play along with Maynard Ferguson and I’m going, “They don’t even have the fingerings in the book for this, so how am I supposed to do this?” You know. So I said, “Well I’ll just use the ones an octave lower.” And then it worked and you know so, and I played in band, in middle school band and when I finally — I remember when I was in middle school band that we were…

started playing and I said what? How come there’s three eighth notes in a beat? I don’t get this. Because it was 6/8 you see. And I didn’t understand how 6/8 worked and — I could play it, because once I heard somebody play it I figured it out you know. But I really was, I mean I always practiced. When I was in junior high school I practiced at least a couple of hours a day. At least. And I listened. See? And I always tell people today, no matter what lessons they’re taking, I say, “Practicing is a good thing.” I…
